feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Severe heatwave warnings cover northern Queensland and the Northern Territory, Australia, to 17 November
entry.summary: Warnings issued on 14 November cover Queensland's Peninsula, Gulf Country and North Tropical Coast and Tablelands, and the Northern Territory's Tiwi and Arnhem districts, with overnight lows in the mid to high 20s °C. — Sources: Australian Bureau of Meteorology, Queensland heatwave warning IDQ21013, issued 14 November 2026 · Australian Bureau of Meteorology, Northern Territory heatwave warning IDD21013, issued 14 November 2026

entry.title: Telfer and Marble Bar in Western Australia reached 44.3 °C on 8 November, the week's highest Australian readings
entry.summary: Fitzroy Crossing reached 44.1 °C on 7 November and Roebourne 43.0 °C on 9 November. Inland, Birdsville reached 42.2 °C and Mount Isa 41.9 °C on 10 November before rain broke the heat in places. — Sources: Australian Bureau of Meteorology, daily weather observations, 7 to 14 November 2026

entry.title: Australia's weekly El Niño ocean index eased to +2.75 °C, and US forecasters still call the event strengthening
entry.summary: The Bureau of Meteorology's relative Niño3.4 index fell from +2.88 °C to +2.75 °C for 2 to 8 November. — Sources: Australian Bureau of Meteorology, weekly relative Niño3.4 index, week of 2 to 8 November 2026 · NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO diagnostic discussion, 12 November 2026

entry.title: Peru's El Niño committee expects coastal heat records and heavy rain on the north coast this summer
entry.summary: Peru's ENFEN said on 13 November that the coastal El Niño stays at extraordinary strength to February 2027. — Sources: ENFEN official communiqué, 13 November 2026, reported by RPP

entry.title: British Columbia, Canada, broke 31 daily high-temperature records on 11 November
entry.summary: Environment and Climate Change Canada counted 31 records broken and one tied. Cache Creek reached 21.5 °C against an old record of 17.0 °C from 1981, and Lillooet beat a record set in 1917. — Sources: Environment and Climate Change Canada, via CP24, 12 November 2026

entry.title: South Africa ran a heatwave to 13 November across North West, the Free State and southern Gauteng
entry.summary: The South African Weather Service warned of a heatwave over North West, most of the Free State, southern Gauteng and the north-eastern Northern Cape, with extremely high fire danger across several provinces. — Sources: South African Weather Service, via IOL, 11 November 2026

entry.title: Lake Kariba fell to 31.67 percent usable storage on 10 November, the reservoir behind Zambia and Zimbabwe's hydropower
entry.summary: The Zambezi River Authority recorded 479.98 metres on 10 November, down from 32.25 percent on 7 November. A year earlier the lake held 8.09 percent. — Sources: Zambezi River Authority, Lake Kariba levels, 7 and 10 November 2026

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany, recovered from 5 centimetres to 73 centimetres in a week
entry.summary: The gauge fell to 5 centimetres overnight on 7 to 8 November and read 73 centimetres at 06:30 on 14 November, which the federal gauge network classes as normal. Rain on the Upper Rhine drove the rise. — Sources: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung, Pegelonline gauge network, readings of 7 to 14 November 2026 · wetter.net, 11 November 2026

entry.title: The Koah fire in Queensland, Australia reached Watch and Act on 13 November before being downgraded
entry.summary: Queensland's fire service put the Koah fire near the Kennedy Highway at Watch and Act, Prepare to Leave, on 13 November. It was downgraded to Advice by the morning of 14 November. — Sources: Queensland Fire Department bushfire alerts, 13 and 14 November 2026 · ABC Emergency, 13 November 2026

entry.title: New South Wales, Australia had a Watch and Act fire near Cessnock on 14 November
entry.summary: The H Pots fire near Cessnock covered 85 hectares and was being controlled. The Sand Track fire had burned 1,401 hectares and stood at Advice. — Sources: NSW Rural Fire Service, major incidents feed, 14 November 2026

entry.title: Brazil's satellites counted 5,657 fire foci from 7 to 13 November, two thirds of them in the Amazon
entry.summary: The Amazon biome had 3,797 foci, the Caatinga 893 and the Cerrado 829. Pará recorded 2,393 and Maranhão 1,069. — Sources: INPE, daily fire foci, reference satellite, 7 to 13 November 2026

entry.title: Indonesia detected 1,118 hotspots in 24 hours on 9 November, and Singapore's air stayed moderate
entry.summary: Southeast Sulawesi, Maluku and South Papua had the most hotspots in Indonesia on 9 November. Singapore's 24-hour PSI read 55 to 78 on 14 November, highest in the west. — Sources: Indonesia Ministry of Forestry SiPongi data, via Katadata, 9 November 2026 · Singapore National Environment Agency, PSI readings, 14 November 2026

entry.title: Maricopa County, Arizona, has confirmed 548 heat-related deaths in 2026
entry.summary: The county counts 316 deaths caused by heat and 232 where heat contributed, with 164 still under investigation. The 2023 record is 645. Reports are now monthly until April. — Sources: Maricopa County Public Health, heat surveillance, week ending 7 November 2026

entry.title: Northern Australia has published no heat-health figures through three weeks of heatwave warnings
entry.summary: No hospital or ambulance heat-presentation figures have been released for Queensland or the Northern Territory during the November warnings. This is an absence of data and says nothing about harm. — Sources: Queensland Health, NT Health and Queensland Ambulance Service publications, searched 14 November 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's latest national count is 425,167 haze-related respiratory infections to 5 November
entry.summary: No newer national figure has been published. The count runs from 20 August and includes 95,627 children under five. Daily new cases are falling except in East Kalimantan. — Sources: Indonesia Ministry of Health, via Bloomberg Technoz, 6 November 2026 · Media Indonesia, November 2026 · Antara, 9 November 2026

entry.title: The Philippines barred penalties on delivery riders who stop work because of heat
entry.summary: Labor Advisory No. 22 requires platforms to assess routes for heat and to reduce, reschedule or suspend assignments by heat-index band. — Sources: Philippine News Agency via SunStar, 12 November 2026, on DOLE Labor Advisory No. 22, series of 2026

entry.title: Safe Work Australia recommends new model regulations for extreme heat at work
entry.summary: Recommendation 20 of Safe Work Australia's Best Practice Review calls for new model work health and safety regulations on extreme heat, air quality and vector-borne disease. — Sources: Safe Work Australia, Best Practice Review final report, October 2026

entry.title: Britain's safety regulator modelled how fast workers in offshore refuges become impaired by heat
entry.summary: HSE research report RR1179, published on 9 November, models the time to heat impairment for workers sheltering in offshore temporary refuges in the United Kingdom. — Sources: Health and Safety Executive, research report RR1179, 9 November 2026
